featured_reviews.review_text:
I came to The PhysioStudio on the recommendation of a doctor friend of mine who herself had been treated by Dr. Shraddha, and honestly, I’m very grateful that I did.

I had been struggling with severe pain and swelling in my left elbow, which had started making even simple daily activities extremely painful and difficult. I had tried multiple treatments before, but everything only gave temporary relief, and I was quite confused and frustrated about what was really causing the problem.

During my sessions, we understood that this may have been connected to an old fracture I had in the same elbow when I was around four years old, which over time had affected the joint. Initially, I was also unsure about the treatment because I had never really heard of fascia release or fascial manipulation before. But to my surprise, the treatment has worked wonderfully for me.

With a combination of fascia release, strengthening and weight-bearing exercises, and ultrasound therapy, I have experienced nearly 70–80% relief in my pain and movement in about 8–9 sessions. The swelling has reduced significantly, and everyday activities feel much easier now.

Dr. Shraddha and Dr Jhanvi have been extremely patient, understanding, and thorough throughout the process. I genuinely feel like I’m healing, not just getting temporary relief. Highly recommend The PhysioStudio to anyone dealing with persistent pain.

With every session, I could feel the improvement. My pain gradually reduced, and my movements became easier. Wearing shoes was the most difficult for me, but that also improved slowly.

Many people ignore strange sensations in their legs until the pain becomes severe. But your body often gives warning signs much earlier.
If you experience tingling in legs, burning sensation in legs, or a constant pins and needles sensation, it could be a sign of nerve pain in leg caused by irritation or compression of nerves.
One of the most common reasons behind these symptoms is sciatica nerve pain, where the sciatic nerve gets irritated in the lower back or hip. This can lead to leg numbness causes, tingling in legs, and sometimes even leg weakness causes. Many people also experience a burning sensation in legs that travels down the thigh or calf.
In some cases, nerve compression symptoms can develop due to prolonged sitting, poor posture, disc irritation, or tight muscles. When the nerve is irritated, it can produce sensations like pins and needles sensation, tingling in legs, or sharp nerve pain in leg.
Another possible reason for these symptoms is peripheral neuropathy symptoms, where nerves become sensitive and start sending abnormal signals like burning sensation in legs, numbness, or weakness.
Sometimes people also notice leg swelling causes along with heaviness and discomfort, which may increase pressure around nerves and worsen sciatica symptoms or nerve compression symptoms.
The good news is that many of these problems can improve with proper physiotherapy for nerve pain.

At first glance, it looks like this person is simply strapped to a moving table... but what if I told you this machine is actually creating space inside the spine to help relieve back pain and sciatica?
What you're seeing is Spinal Decompression Therapy, a specialized non-surgical treatment commonly used for people suffering from chronic lower back pain, sciatica, bulging discs, herniated discs, and certain degenerative spinal conditions.
So how does it work?
The motorized table applies a gentle, controlled pulling force to the lumbar spine (lower back). This creates a process called **decompression**, where the vertebrae are slightly separated, reducing pressure on the spinal discs and nearby nerves.
Why is this important?
🦴 Reduces Disc Pressure
Spinal discs act as shock absorbers between your vertebrae. When a disc bulges or herniates, it can press on nearby nerves and cause pain, numbness, or tingling down the leg. Decompression may help reduce this pressure.
💧 Improves Nutrient Exchange
Unlike many tissues in the body, spinal discs have a very limited blood supply. The gentle stretching and relaxation cycles help encourage the movement of water, oxygen, and nutrients into the discs, supporting their health and recovery.
While spinal decompression can be beneficial for the right patient, it isn't a one-size-fits-all solution. A proper assessment is always important to determine the root cause of your pain.

Frozen Shoulder (Adhesive Capsulitis) is more than just shoulder pain or muscle tightness.
Many people believe it develops from overuse, but the real problem often occurs inside the shoulder joint capsule.
As inflammation builds, the capsule gradually thickens and stiffens, leading to shoulder stiffness, limited shoulder mobility, and difficulty performing simple daily activities like reaching overhead, dressing, or sleeping comfortably.
What makes frozen shoulder unique is its strong association with diabetes, thyroid disorders, and hormonal changes. These underlying conditions can influence the tissues surrounding the joint and increase the risk of developing adhesive capsulitis.
The good news? Early clinical assessment and the right physiotherapy approach can help manage pain, improve shoulder mobility, restore movement, and support shoulder rehabilitation.
Treatment is most effective when tailored to the stage of the condition rather than using the same exercises for everyone.

A controlled traction technique helps decompress the joint surfaces, allowing them to move more freely with less restriction.

When joints become stiff, your body starts compensating during walking, squatting, climbing stairs, and even simple daily activities. Over time, these movement compensations can contribute to discomfort, reduced mobility, and unnecessary strain on surrounding muscles.
